newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE July canola falls C$10/T limit on commercials.
newsitem.headline: WCE July canola falls C$10/T limit on commercials.

text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange July canola futures sank the C$10-per-tonne limit to C$373 a tonne on commercial selling early in the session, spurred by commercial selling and a sharp drop in CBOT soybeans, traders said.
"Everybody's selling, commercials, commission houses, locals but it's mainly commercials selling because of the fall in the beans," a trader said.

The U.S. Agriculture Department issued ending stocks and acreage estimates earlier Monday for major U.S. crops. Soybean acreage, tabbed at 70.85 million acres, was greater than expected and deemed bearish by U.S. traders.
All WCE contracts posted new lows with the July at C$373 per tonne, August down C$9.30 at C$365.80, November down C$8.80 at C$347.50 and January down C$6.50 at C$351.50.
